parts.readText:
Chen Shu-chu: A Vegetable Seller Who Gave

WORDS TO KNOW
donation - money given to help
influential - able to affect others
generous - willing to give
extraordinary - very unusual or special

[1] Helping others does not always begin with a large amount of money. Sometimes, it begins with an ordinary person who decides to share. Chen Shu-chu, a vegetable seller in Taitung, Taiwan, became known for doing just that.

[2] Chen's family did not have much money. When she was thirteen, her mother became seriously ill. Her father tried to borrow money for hospital treatment, but her mother died. After elementary school, Chen helped her father sell vegetables to support the family. Later, when one of her brothers became ill, her former school raised money to help. Her brother did not survive, but Chen remembered the kindness people had shown her family.

[3] For many years, Chen worked long hours at her vegetable stand. She lived simply and saved money from her work. She used her savings to help children and schools. One of her donations helped build a library at her former elementary school. Other donations supported children who needed food, a safe place to live, or help staying in school.

[4] In 2010, TIME magazine included Chen on its list of the world's 100 most influential people. Two years later, she received the Ramon Magsaysay Award for helping others. She donated the entire cash prize to a hospital in Taitung. Even an award became another opportunity to give.

[5] Chen did not see herself as an extraordinary person. She believed that being willing to help mattered, even when someone could give only a little. Her life shows how years of ordinary work and generous choices can make a difference.

parts.title: Part B | Short Answer
parts.instruction: Directions: Answer in complete sentences. Support your answers with details from the selection.

questions.q: How did Chen's choices about work and daily living allow her to help others? Include two details.
questions.keyPoints: She worked long hours at her vegetable stand, lived simply and saved money, and used those savings to help children and schools (for example, helping build a library at her former elementary school, or supporting children who needed food, a safe place to live, or help staying in school).

questions.q: Someone says, "Chen helped people only because she wanted an award." Explain why the selection does not support this idea. Use text evidence.
questions.keyPoints: She helped for years before any award. After winning the Ramon Magsaysay Award she donated the entire cash prize to a hospital in Taitung, and she did not see herself as extraordinary — she believed being willing to help mattered even when someone could give only a little.

parts.title: Part C | Analyze Main Idea and Details
parts.instruction: Directions: Write the main idea of the whole selection. Then add three different key details that support it.

questions.q: Main Idea: Write the main idea of the whole selection.
questions.keyPoints: Ordinary people like Chen can make a difference by choosing to share and help others, even when they can give only a little.
Any detail that supports the main idea, e.g. Chen worked long hours, lived simply and saved money from her work to help others.
e.g. One of her donations helped build a library at her former elementary school; other donations supported children who needed food, a safe place to live, or help staying in school.
e.g. She donated the entire cash prize of the Ramon Magsaysay Award to a hospital in Taitung; TIME named her one of the 100 most influential people in 2010.

parts.title: Part D | Generate Questions
parts.instruction: Directions: Read each detail. Write a question that the detail answers. Then write one interview question.

questions.q:
Detail: Chen helped her father sell vegetables to support her family.
Question:
questions.keyPoints: e.g. Why did Chen help her father sell vegetables? / How did Chen help her family after elementary school?

questions.q:
Detail: One of Chen's donations helped build a library at her former elementary school.
Question:
questions.keyPoints: e.g. What did one of Chen's donations help build? / How did Chen help her former school?

questions.q:
Imagine you could interview Chen. Write one question about her decision to help others. Do not ask a question already answered directly in the selection.
Interview Question:
questions.keyPoints: A question about WHY or HOW she decided to help that is NOT answered directly in the text, e.g. "What made you decide to keep giving even when you had little money yourself?"
